title: Promise and Summer
premise: Wendell Dunmore ghostwrites the memoirs of festival founder Elias Vane, a man whose charm hides a fifteen-year-old betrayal. When a letter postmarked eleven years ago surfaces in a box of Elias's papers, it reveals that Wendell's former partner, June Calloway, never abandoned them — she was driven out by Elias, who threatened to expose Wendell's past crime of survival. As the summer solstice festival approaches, Wendell must choose between the safe life they've built and confronting Elias publicly, while June returns to town to finally hear the sentence Wendell has rehearsed for a decade: 'I chose you, and I was wrong to let them take that choice from me.' The book ends at the festival's closing night, where Wendell speaks the truth on stage, Elias falls, and Wendell and June walk out together into the dark — poorer, freer, and finally whole.
about_author: Oscar Winterbourne is the pen name of a former small-town newspaper reporter who spent a decade writing other people's stories before claiming one as their own. They live near water, keep an unsent letter in a desk drawer, and write only in summer.

chapters.title: The Ghost in the Manuscript
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Wendell drafts another chapter of Elias Vane's memoirs, polishing lies into gold, and reflects on the fifteen years of careful, small steps since their own disgrace. Emotional beat: quiet self-erasure, the ache of invisible labor.

chapters.title: Box 47
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Sorting Elias's archives for source material, Wendell finds an unopened letter postmarked eleven years ago, addressed to them in June's handwriting. They don't open it. Emotional beat: dread disguised as caution.

chapters.title: What the Town Remembers
chapters.summary: June's POV. June returns to Harborlight for the solstice festival, telling herself it's closure, not hope. Old neighbors greet her with warmth and suspicion in equal measure. Emotional beat: homesickness for a place that exiled you.

chapters.title: Eleven Years of Silence
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Alone at night, Wendell finally opens the letter: June never left by choice; someone forced her out. The handwriting shakes; so does Wendell. Emotional beat: the floor giving way beneath a carefully built life.

chapters.title: Elias at Breakfast
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Wendell watches Elias perform charm over coffee, testing him with oblique questions about eleven years ago. Elias deflects beautifully, and Wendell recognizes the technique — it's one they taught him. Emotional beat: cold clarity.

chapters.title: The Rehearsed Sentence
chapters.summary: June's POV. In her motel room, June rereads her own old letter and admits why she came back: not for answers, but to hear Wendell say the thing they never said. Emotional beat: guarded longing.

chapters.title: Small Safe Steps
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Wendell inventories everything they could lose — the contract, the apartment, the anonymity — and almost burns the letter. Almost. Emotional beat: terror masquerading as pragmatism.

chapters.title: First Sight
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Wendell and June see each other across the festival grounds mid-setup, neither approaching. A shared look lasts three seconds and rearranges eleven years. Emotional beat: suspended breath.

chapters.title: The Version He Wrote
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Reading Elias's memoir draft, Wendell finds the chapter about 'the unfortunate incident' — Elias's sanitized account of how June was driven away and Wendell's crime buried. Emotional beat: fury sharpening into purpose.

chapters.title: Coffee, No Promises
chapters.summary: June's POV. June and Wendell meet at the dockside café, circling each other with decade-old wounds. June asks one question: 'Did you know?' Wendell can't yet answer honestly. Emotional beat: love and resentment sharing a table.

chapters.title: What Survival Cost
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Flashback woven through present: the crime Wendell committed at nineteen to survive, the leverage Elias has held ever since, the deal that bought silence. Emotional beat: grief for their younger self.

chapters.title: The Festival Opens
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. Lanterns rise over Harborlight; Elias gives his opening speech to adoring crowds while Wendell stands in the wings holding evidence like a lit fuse. Emotional beat: public splendor, private vertigo.

chapters.title: June's Evidence
chapters.summary: June's POV. June reveals she kept records too — letters, dates, a witness to Elias's threat. Together the two accounts form a case. Emotional beat: two halves of a truth clicking together.

chapters.title: The Offer
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Elias, sensing danger, offers Wendell co-authorship, money, and a clean slate if the letter stays buried. For one hour, Wendell is tempted. Emotional beat: the price of survival made literal.

chapters.title: Refusal
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Wendell declines, walks out of Elias's house, and calls June from the seawall: 'I'm done being safe.' Emotional beat: exhilaration laced with fear.

chapters.title: Elias Strikes
chapters.summary: June's POV. Elias threatens to expose Wendell's old crime publicly unless June leaves again by morning. June photographs the threat instead. Emotional beat: recognition that he'll always reach for the same weapon.

chapters.title: Night Before the Closing
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Wendell and June sit up all night drafting what will be said tomorrow, and Wendell practices the rehearsed sentence aloud for the first time, voice breaking on the second word. Emotional beat: tenderness forged under pressure.

chapters.title: Closing Night
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. On the festival stage, before the whole town, Wendell abandons the prepared remarks and tells the truth: the crime, the blackmail, what Elias did to June. Emotional beat: terror transfigured into release.

chapters.title: The Fall
chapters.summary: June's POV. The crowd turns; Elias's patronage evaporates in real time; he lunges for the microphone and finds no one willing to hand it back. Justice arrives outside any courtroom. Emotional beat: righteous, sobering collapse.

chapters.title: The Sentence
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Away from the stage, in the lantern light, Wendell says the full rehearsed sentence to June — the choice, the apology, the love that never left. Emotional beat: ten years exhaling at once.

chapters.title: After
chapters.summary: June's POV. Days later: consequences settle, contracts dissolve, the town recalibrates. June and Wendell begin the unglamorous work of rebuilding — this time visibly, together. Emotional beat: fragile, practical hope.

chapters.title: Promise and Summer
chapters.summary: Shared POV, alternating paragraphs. On the last night of the season, they walk the empty festival grounds, and Wendell writes their own name on a page for the first time in fifteen years. Emotional beat: arrival — the story was never about the letter, but the voice that finally claimed it.
